annotationRationale: Prime-power restrictions from overlapping gcd conditions force the exact powers of 2 and 3 in gcd(d,a). The meaning of greatest common divisor supports these deductions.
sourceMethod: Follows the official prime-factor argument, expanding why a cannot contain 3^2 and d cannot contain 2^2 before restricting the remaining factor to 13.

review.mathCheck: The overlapping gcd conditions force exactly one factor of 3 in a and exactly one factor of 2 in d. Since \(8\mid a\) and \(27\mid d\), their gcd is \(6m\) with m divisible by neither 2 nor 3. The interval permits \(m=12,13,14,15,16\), leaving only 13. Thus \(13\mid a\), choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA Q22 on page 11, with expanded justification of the prime-power restrictions. Omitting the official existence example does not weaken the required must-divide deduction.
review.annotationCheck: Prime-exponent structure is appropriately assessed, while the elementary meaning of gcd supports the deductions. No missing case or unjustified restriction affects the conclusion.
